questions.question: What useful things do we get when fuels burn, and what else does burning produce?
questions.expected_answer: We get heat, for cooking, warming homes and making electricity, and light, for seeing in the dark. Burning also produces smoke, ash and gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour.

questions.question: Why must a fire be built with paper and kindling first, before adding logs?
questions.expected_answer: A fuel must be heated to a high enough temperature to ignite. Paper ignites easily from a match. Burning paper heats the kindling until it ignites, and the kindling heats the bigger sticks and logs, which need much more heat to ignite.

questions.question: Explain the candle and jar test and what the fire triangle shows.
questions.expected_answer: When a jar is placed over a burning candle, the flame gets smaller and goes out, because it uses up the oxygen and no fresh air can get in. Candles in the open keep burning. The fire triangle shows that a fire needs fuel, heat and oxygen; taking away any one puts it out.
